\newcommand{\ealkey}[1]{\textcolor{ealkeycolour}{#1}}

% One translated word above one English word. Built from kernel
% primitives, never a tabular, which would break wherever the sheet
% loads array, booktabs or tabularx. The box is as wide as the wider of
% the two, so a long translation pushes its neighbours aside instead of
% overlapping them, and it claims its full height so a table row or a
% TikZ node makes room for it.
\newcommand{\ealgloss}[2]{%
  \sbox{\ealboxen}{\ealkey{#1}}%
  \sbox{\ealboxtr}{\small\textcolor{ealtwocolour}{\ealtext{#2}}}%
  \setlength{\ealglosswd}{\wd\ealboxen}%
  \ifdim\wd\ealboxtr>\ealglosswd\setlength{\ealglosswd}{\wd\ealboxtr}\fi
  \leavevmode
  \makebox[\ealglosswd][c]{%
    \makebox[0pt][c]{\usebox{\ealboxen}}%
    \makebox[0pt][c]{\raisebox{\ealglossraise}{\usebox{\ealboxtr}}}%
  }%
}

% opens up line spacing around a block of glosses, so the raised
% translations sit clear of the line above
\newenvironment{ealglossed}{\par\linespread{2.1}\selectfont\ignorespaces}{\par}

% a whole translated sentence above its English counterpart. block level,
% so it does not belong inside a tabular cell
\newcommand{\ealpara}[2]{%
  \par\addvspace{0.5\baselineskip}%
  {\color{ealtwocolour}\ealtextblock{#1}}%
  \penalty200
  {\color{ealenglish}#2\par}%
  \addvspace{0.5\baselineskip}%
}

{\small \begin{enumerate}[label=\textbf{\arabic*.}, leftmargin=*, itemsep=5pt, topsep=4pt, start=1]
\item \dial{FORWARD}{1}{WEEK} \quad Day and date: \lline
\item \dial{FORWARD}{10}{DAYS} \quad Day and date: \lline
\item \dial{BACK}{2}{WEEKS} \quad Day and date: \lline
\item \dial{FORWARD}{3 WEEKS}{+ 2 DAYS} \quad Day and date: \lline
\item \dial{BACK}{45}{DAYS} \quad Day and date: \lline
\item \dial{FORWARD}{100}{HOURS} \quad Day, date \emph{and time}: \lline
\item Dr Chrono wants to watch the fireworks on Bonfire Night (5 November) and then jump to Christmas Day (25 December). How many days forward is that? \aline\ \ Write it in weeks and days: \aline
\item The dial gets stuck so it can only jump in \textbf{whole weeks}. Starting from today, can Dr Chrono land exactly on Christmas Day? Explain, and say which two dates nearest Christmas it \emph{can} reach.\par\vspace{4pt}\rule{\linewidth}{0.4pt}
\item \textbf{Spooky landing:} Dr Chrono's machine always breaks down on a Friday the 13th. Which date on these \ealgloss{calendars}{kalendarzach} should she avoid? \lline
\end{enumerate}}

  \draw[up, ttglow!80!black] ($(\b.south west)$) to[bend left=35] node[below, lab, text=ttglow!70!black]{$\times\k$} ($(\a.south east)$);}

\end{tikzpicture}\end{minipage}\hfill\begin{minipage}[c]{0.32\linewidth}\factbox{5.4cm}{\ealgloss{\textbf{Leap years}}{lata przestępne}\\ A normal year has 365 days. A \ealgloss{\textbf{leap year}}{rok przestępny} has 366 (it has 29 February).\\[3pt]\ealgloss{Leap years}{lata przestępne} are \ealgloss{divisible}{podzielne} by 4 \ldots\ \emph{except} \ealgloss{century years}{lat kończących się na 00} (like 1900), which must be \ealgloss{divisible}{podzielne} by 400.}\end{minipage}\par\medskip
{\small\textbf{1.}\ Convert:\par\smallskip\begin{tabular}{rclp{1.6cm}p{0.6cm}rcll}3 weeks & = & \rule{1.6cm}{0.4pt} & days && 4 \ealgloss{centuries}{wieki} & = & \rule{1.6cm}{0.4pt} & \ealgloss{decades}{dekad}\\[10pt]
2 days & = & \rule{1.6cm}{0.4pt} & hours && 2 \ealgloss{millennia}{tysiąclecia} & = & \rule{1.6cm}{0.4pt} & \ealgloss{centuries}{wieków}\\[10pt]
180 minutes & = & \rule{1.6cm}{0.4pt} & hours && 7200 seconds & = & \rule{1.6cm}{0.4pt} & hours\\[10pt]
5 \ealgloss{decades}{dekad} & = & \rule{1.6cm}{0.4pt} & years && 3 days & = & \rule{1.6cm}{0.4pt} & minutes\\[10pt]\end{tabular}}\par\medskip
{\small \begin{enumerate}[label=\textbf{\arabic*.}, leftmargin=*, itemsep=5pt, topsep=4pt, start=2]
\item Write each dial reading in a more sensible way.\par\smallskip\begin{tabular}{@{}ll}\dial{FORWARD}{72}{HOURS} & = \rule{3.5cm}{0.4pt} days\\[5pt]\dial{FORWARD}{420}{DAYS} & = \rule{3.5cm}{0.4pt} weeks\\[5pt]\dial{BACK}{1000}{HOURS} & = \rule{1.5cm}{0.4pt} days and \rule{1.5cm}{0.4pt} hours\\[5pt]\dial{BACK}{1000000}{SECONDS} & \textbf{Challenge:} = \rule{0.8cm}{0.4pt} d \rule{0.8cm}{0.4pt} h \rule{0.8cm}{0.4pt} min \rule{0.8cm}{0.4pt} s\end{tabular}
\item Dr Chrono lands on \textbf{29 February}. Which of these years could it be? Circle them: \quad 2028 \quad 2030 \quad 2100 \quad 2400
\item Put these jumps in order from \textbf{shortest} to \textbf{longest}:\par\smallskip\dial{JUMP}{1000}{HOURS}\ \ \dial{JUMP}{6}{WEEKS}\ \ \dial{JUMP}{50000}{MINUTES}\par\smallskip\dial{JUMP}{1000000}{SECONDS}\ \ \dial{JUMP}{0.1}{YEARS}\par\vspace{6pt}\rule{\linewidth}{0.4pt}
\end{enumerate}}
\clearpage
\banner{Part C \quad \ealgloss{Timeline}{Oś czasu} jumps --- giant leaps}\par\smallskip
\noindent\begin{minipage}[c]{0.44\linewidth}{\small For really big jumps, Dr Chrono uses \ealgloss{timelines}{osi czasu}. Years \ealgloss{\textbf{BC}}{p.n.e.} count \emph{backwards}: 2560 \ealgloss{BC}{p.n.e.} is further in the past than 776 \ealgloss{BC}{p.n.e.}. Years \ealgloss{\textbf{AD}}{n.e.} count forwards from \ealgloss{AD}{n.e.} 1.}\end{minipage}\hfill\begin{minipage}[c]{0.54\linewidth}\factbox{9.3cm}{\textbf{Watch out: there is no year 0!} 1 \ealgloss{BC}{p.n.e.} is followed straight away by \ealgloss{AD}{n.e.} 1.\\[2pt]\emph{Example:} from 776 \ealgloss{BC}{p.n.e.} to \ealgloss{AD}{n.e.} 43.\\ 776 \ealgloss{BC}{p.n.e.} $\to$ 1 \ealgloss{BC}{p.n.e.} is 775 years; 1 \ealgloss{BC}{p.n.e.} $\to$ \ealgloss{AD}{n.e.} 1 is 1 year; \ealgloss{AD}{n.e.} 1 $\to$ \ealgloss{AD}{n.e.} 43 is 42 years.\\Total $= 775 + 1 + 42 = \mathbf{818}$ years. \quad Shortcut: $776 + 43 - 1$.}\end{minipage}\par\medskip

\banner{Part D \quad Mission log --- getting home}\par\smallskip
{\small Dr Chrono sets off from \textbf{\ealgloss{AD}{n.e.} 2026} and makes four jumps. Her battery starts at \textbf{100\%}, and every \ealgloss{\textbf{century}}{wiek} of travel (forwards or backwards) uses \textbf{2\%} of the battery.}\par\medskip
\begin{center}{\small\begin{tabular}{c|c|p{3.2cm}|p{3.2cm}}\textbf{Jump} & \textbf{Dial} & \textbf{From} & \textbf{Lands in}\\\hline
1 & \dial{BACK}{3}{\ealgloss{CENTURIES}{wieki}} & \ealgloss{AD}{n.e.} 2026 & \\[10pt]\hline
2 & \dial{FORWARD}{25}{YEARS} &  & \\[10pt]\hline
3 & \dial{BACK}{2}{\ealgloss{MILLENNIA}{tysiąclecia}} &  & \\[10pt]\hline
4 & \dial{FORWARD}{1500}{YEARS} &  & \\[10pt]\hline\end{tabular}}\end{center}
{\small \begin{enumerate}[label=\textbf{\arabic*.}, leftmargin=*, itemsep=5pt, topsep=4pt, start=1]
\item What single jump would take Dr Chrono straight home to \ealgloss{AD}{n.e.} 2026? \par\smallskip FORWARD or BACK? \aline\quad How many years? \aline
\item How many years did she travel in jumps 1--4 altogether? \aline\quad How many \ealgloss{centuries}{wieków} is that? \aline
\item How much battery has she used so far? \aline\quad How much is left? \aline
\item Does she have enough battery to make the jump home? Show your working.\par\vspace{4pt}\rule{\linewidth}{0.4pt}
\item \textbf{Design a mission:} plan three jumps that visit the Great Pyramid, the Battle of Hastings and the Moon landing, then come home. Write your dial settings and work out the battery used.\par\medskip\begin{center}\begin{tabular}{c|p{3.4cm}|p{3.4cm}|p{3.4cm}}\textbf{Jump} & \textbf{Dial setting} & \textbf{Lands in} & \textbf{Battery used}\\\hline1 & & & \\[10pt]\hline 2 & & & \\[10pt]\hline 3 & & & \\[10pt]\hline Home & & & \\[10pt]\hline\multicolumn{3}{r|}{\textbf{Total battery used}} & \\[10pt]\hline\end{tabular}\end{center}
\end{enumerate}}
\clearpage\enlargethispage{3\baselineskip}\begin{center}{\LARGE\bfseries Answers}\end{center}\vspace{-6pt}
\banner{Part A \quad \ealgloss{Calendar}{Kalendarz} hops --- small jumps}\par\smallskip
{\small \begin{enumerate}[label=\textbf{\arabic*.}, leftmargin=*, itemsep=5pt, topsep=4pt, start=1]
\item \dial{FORWARD}{1}{WEEK} \quad Day and date: \lline\par\ans{Saturday 7 November 2026}
\item \dial{FORWARD}{10}{DAYS} \quad Day and date: \lline\par\ans{Tuesday 10 November 2026}
\item \dial{BACK}{2}{WEEKS} \quad Day and date: \lline\par\ans{Saturday 17 October 2026}
\item \dial{FORWARD}{3 WEEKS}{+ 2 DAYS} \quad Day and date: \lline\par\ans{Monday 23 November 2026}
\item \dial{BACK}{45}{DAYS} \quad Day and date: \lline\par\ans{Wednesday 16 September 2026}
\item \dial{FORWARD}{100}{HOURS} \quad Day, date \emph{and time}: \lline\par\ans{Wednesday 4 November 2026 at 14:00 (100 hours = 4 days 4 hours)}
\item Dr Chrono wants to watch the fireworks on Bonfire Night (5 November) and then jump to Christmas Day (25 December). How many days forward is that? \aline\ \ Write it in weeks and days: \aline\par\ans{50 days = 7 weeks 1 day}
\item The dial gets stuck so it can only jump in \textbf{whole weeks}. Starting from today, can Dr Chrono land exactly on Christmas Day? Explain, and say which two dates nearest Christmas it \emph{can} reach.\par\vspace{4pt}\rule{\linewidth}{0.4pt}\par\ans{No. 31 Oct to 25 Dec is 55 days, not a \ealgloss{multiple}{wielokrotnością} of 7. Whole weeks from a Saturday always land on a Saturday: Sat 19 Dec (7 weeks) or Sat 26 Dec (8 weeks).}
\item \textbf{Spooky landing:} Dr Chrono's machine always breaks down on a Friday the 13th. Which date on these \ealgloss{calendars}{kalendarzach} should she avoid? \lline\par\ans{Friday 13 November 2026}
\end{enumerate}}
\banner{Part B \quad \ealgloss{Conversion}{Zamiana} station --- medium jumps}\par\smallskip
{\small\textbf{1.}\ Convert:\par\smallskip\begin{tabular}{rclp{1.6cm}p{0.6cm}rcll}3 weeks & = & \ans{21} & days && 4 \ealgloss{centuries}{wieki} & = & \ans{40} & \ealgloss{decades}{dekad}\\[10pt]
2 days & = & \ans{48} & hours && 2 \ealgloss{millennia}{tysiąclecia} & = & \ans{20} & \ealgloss{centuries}{wieków}\\[10pt]
180 minutes & = & \ans{3} & hours && 7200 seconds & = & \ans{2} & hours\\[10pt]
5 \ealgloss{decades}{dekad} & = & \ans{50} & years && 3 days & = & \ans{4320} & minutes\\[10pt]\end{tabular}}\par\medskip
{\small \begin{enumerate}[label=\textbf{\arabic*.}, leftmargin=*, itemsep=5pt, topsep=4pt, start=2]
\item Write each dial reading in a more sensible way.\par\smallskip\begin{tabular}{@{}ll}\dial{FORWARD}{72}{HOURS} & = \rule{3.5cm}{0.4pt} days\\[5pt]\dial{FORWARD}{420}{DAYS} & = \rule{3.5cm}{0.4pt} weeks\\[5pt]\dial{BACK}{1000}{HOURS} & = \rule{1.5cm}{0.4pt} days and \rule{1.5cm}{0.4pt} hours\\[5pt]\dial{BACK}{1000000}{SECONDS} & \textbf{Challenge:} = \rule{0.8cm}{0.4pt} d \rule{0.8cm}{0.4pt} h \rule{0.8cm}{0.4pt} min \rule{0.8cm}{0.4pt} s\end{tabular}\par\ans{3 days;\quad 60 weeks;\quad 41 days 16 hours;\quad 11 d 13 h 46 min 40 s}
\item Dr Chrono lands on \textbf{29 February}. Which of these years could it be? Circle them: \quad 2028 \quad 2030 \quad 2100 \quad 2400\par\ans{2028 and 2400 (2030 is not \ealgloss{divisible}{podzielny} by 4; 2100 is a \ealgloss{century year}{rokiem kończącym się na 00} not \ealgloss{divisible}{podzielny} by 400)}
\item Put these jumps in order from \textbf{shortest} to \textbf{longest}:\par\smallskip\dial{JUMP}{1000}{HOURS}\ \ \dial{JUMP}{6}{WEEKS}\ \ \dial{JUMP}{50000}{MINUTES}\par\smallskip\dial{JUMP}{1000000}{SECONDS}\ \ \dial{JUMP}{0.1}{YEARS}\par\vspace{6pt}\rule{\linewidth}{0.4pt}\par\ans{1\,000\,000 s ($\approx$ 11.6 days) $<$ 50\,000 min ($\approx$ 34.7 days) $<$ 0.1 years (36.5 days) $<$ 1000 hours ($\approx$ 41.7 days) $<$ 6 weeks (42 days)}
\end{enumerate}}

\item How many years ago (from 2026) was \ldots\par\smallskip\begin{tabular}{@{}l@{\ }l@{\qquad}l@{\ }l}(a) the Battle of Hastings? & \aline & (b) the Roman invasion? & \aline\\[5pt](c) the first Olympic Games? & \aline & (d) the Great Pyramid? & \aline\end{tabular}\par\ans{(a) 960 years \quad (b) 1983 years \quad (c) 2026 + 776 $-$ 1 = 2801 years \quad (d) 2026 + 2560 $-$ 1 = 4585 years}
\item Write your answer to 2(a) in \ealgloss{centuries}{wiekach} and \ealgloss{decades}{dekadach}: \lline\par\ans{9 \ealgloss{centuries}{wieków} and 6 \ealgloss{decades}{dekad}}
\item Where (when!) does the machine land? Mark these on the big \ealgloss{timeline}{osi czasu} too.\par\smallskip\begin{tabular}{@{}l@{\ }l}from 2026: \dial{BACK}{3}{\ealgloss{MILLENNIA}{tysiąclecia}} & lands in \lline\\[10pt]from 2026: \dial{FORWARD}{5}{\ealgloss{CENTURIES}{wieków}} & lands in \lline\\[10pt]from 2026: \dial{BACK}{25}{\ealgloss{CENTURIES}{wieków}} & lands in \lline\end{tabular}\par\ans{975 \ealgloss{BC}{p.n.e.} \quad (check: 975 + 2026 $-$ 1 = 3000); \quad \ealgloss{AD}{n.e.} 2526; \quad 475 \ealgloss{BC}{p.n.e.} (2500 $-$ 2026 + 1 = 475)}
\item \textbf{Zoom in:} mark these on the zoomed \ealgloss{timeline}{osi czasu}: \quad Magna Carta \textbf{1215} \quad Great Fire of London \textbf{1666} \quad Moon landing \textbf{1969} \quad Today \textbf{2026}\par\ans{see crosses on the zoomed \ealgloss{timeline}{osi czasu}}
\item How many years from (a) Magna Carta to the Great Fire? \aline\quad (b) the Moon landing to today? \aline\par\ans{(a) 451 years \quad (b) 57 years}
\item Is the Great Fire of London closer in time to the Battle of Hastings, or to today? Show how you know.\par\vspace{4pt}\rule{\linewidth}{0.4pt}\par\ans{Today: 2026 $-$ 1666 = 360 years, but 1666 $-$ 1066 = 600 years.}

{\small \begin{enumerate}[label=\textbf{\arabic*.}, leftmargin=*, itemsep=5pt, topsep=4pt, start=1]
\item What single jump would take Dr Chrono straight home to \ealgloss{AD}{n.e.} 2026? \par\smallskip FORWARD or BACK? \aline\quad How many years? \aline\par\ans{FORWARD 775 years (\ealgloss{AD}{n.e.} 1251 to \ealgloss{AD}{n.e.} 2026)}
\item How many years did she travel in jumps 1--4 altogether? \aline\quad How many \ealgloss{centuries}{wieków} is that? \aline\par\ans{300 + 25 + 2000 + 1500 = 3825 years = 38.25 \ealgloss{centuries}{wieku}}
\item How much battery has she used so far? \aline\quad How much is left? \aline\par\ans{38.25 $\times$ 2\% = 76.5\% used, so 23.5\% left}
\item Does she have enough battery to make the jump home? Show your working.\par\vspace{4pt}\rule{\linewidth}{0.4pt}\par\ans{Yes. 775 years = 7.75 \ealgloss{centuries}{wieku}, which needs 7.75 $\times$ 2\% = 15.5\%, and 23.5\% $>$ 15.5\%. She gets home with 8\% left.}
\item \textbf{Design a mission:} plan three jumps that visit the Great Pyramid, the Battle of Hastings and the Moon landing, then come home. Write your dial settings and work out the battery used.\par\medskip\begin{center}\begin{tabular}{c|p{3.4cm}|p{3.4cm}|p{3.4cm}}\textbf{Jump} & \textbf{Dial setting} & \textbf{Lands in} & \textbf{Battery used}\\\hline1 & & & \\[10pt]\hline 2 & & & \\[10pt]\hline 3 & & & \\[10pt]\hline Home & & & \\[10pt]\hline\multicolumn{3}{r|}{\textbf{Total battery used}} & \\[10pt]\hline\end{tabular}\end{center}\par\ans{e.g.\ BACK 4585 years (to 2560 \ealgloss{BC}{p.n.e.}), FORWARD 3625 years (to 1066), FORWARD 903 years (to 1969), FORWARD 57 years (home). Total 9170 years = 91.7 \ealgloss{centuries}{wieku}, so 183.4\% of battery: she would need to recharge!}}
